capabilities: Answer vault questions with click-to-source citations via local RAG
Download, run, and place local models across GPUs, or reuse Ollama and LM Studio
Crawl websites into the vault as offline markdown notes
Generate a citation-checked wiki from indexed content
Index PDFs, Office files, ebooks, code, and scanned pages via OCR
extras: First launch downloads a server binary (a few hundred MB) plus models of hundreds of MB to several GB each; the macOS binary is unsigned and the plugin clears the quarantine flag. Server and model cache live outside the vault and need a manual uninstall step. The manifest notes the plugin has not been manually reviewed by Obsidian staff, and the README explains why the store's automated review flags shell and filesystem access.
motivation: The author argues a vault is already a curated document set, ideal for a local retrieval-augmented search engine you build yourself.
problem: Obsidian has no built-in way to ask questions across the vault with verifiable citations or to run and manage local LLMs from inside the app.

relations.evidence: No Ollama required, but lilbee uses your Ollama, LM Studio, or cloud models if you have them.
If your models already live in Ollama or LM Studio, point lilbee at the running server.
Install a coding-agent plugin like Claudian alongside lilbee and pair them in one click
It browses featured picks or searches Hugging Face Hub.

summary: Local AI search engine and LLM manager that indexes the vault for cited RAG chat, and adds a web crawler, model catalog, and auto-generated wiki.
